reason: Re-opened packet.js quran 23 --verse 10.58: al-Tabari’s own opening gloss is there verbatim (bounty = Islam, mercy = the Qur’an, which He sent down), and it is his own reading; he reports the reverse view (bounty = Qur’an, mercy = Islam) without ruling between the meanings, and his closing tarjih is on the reading with ya’, so ‘reads’ (not ‘prefers’) is right. But the last clause drifts: he says the Islam He called them to and the Qur’an He sent down, jointly, are better than the debris of this world, its wealth and treasures, that they amass (one predicate on a joined subject, following the singular huwa khayr). ‘each worth more’ asserts a separate comparison for each that his words do not make. Small, and fixable in one word. Everything else holds: plain sense matches day.js (10:57 exhortation and balm announced to mankind, 10:58 ‘Say’), verse.js ok (Yunus 10:58), entry-check ok on the shipped and on the corrected sentence.
better: Just after an exhortation and a balm for the breasts is announced to mankind, the Prophet is told what to say; al-Tabari, on 10:58, reads the bounty as Islam and the mercy as the Qur’an, together worth more than this world’s wealth and treasure. (entry-check ok; same src and evidence)
